_comment: SHARED FIXTURE (NRM-2, the CURRENT format) — two independent implementations must agree on
Rust  : nmts/crypto/tests/api.rs        (what the standalone recovery tool will parse)
The browser assembles the manifest JSON itself because the document contains every file
key and therefore may never leave the crypto worker in the clear. That makes this file the
contract between the writer and the reader. Both sides compare PARSED values, not bytes, so
key order is free; field names and shapes are not.
Keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored by both parsers.
Covers: the chain fields, a multi-part file with no quilt, a quilted file, an item with no
content hash (committed before hashes existed), a part with no Sui object id, a part that
NAMES its storage network, and a part that omits it (= walrus, what pre-field maps look like).
The 'filecoin' value below is a FORMAT PROBE, not a claim that anything is stored there — a
non-default name is what stops either side passing this test with 'walrus' hardcoded.
NRM-2 added part_index, required on every part and equal to that part's own position in the
array (RECOVERY-MANIFEST.md 2.1). It is spelled out here rather than derived so that a wrong
number is caught by a written value instead of by a loop that would agree with itself.
